Data collected by Anselmi & Wickelmaier, Univ. Tuebingen, Feb-Mar 2010; paper Heller & Wickelmaier (2013) doi:10.1016/j.endm.2013.05.145 (not reachable: Elsevier API/ScienceDirect returned no article text).
note: Item codes b101-b112/b201-b212 are the pks data's own scored-column names (data/pks.R: resp = x[,item], id = row index 1..504, wave 0/1 = before/after the learning object); the manual prints each problem's wording under the parallel raw-answer column p101-p212 and describes b1xx/b2xx as the same problems coded correct (1) or error (0). The bNNN<->pNNN tie was verified by rescoring (verify_pks_probability.R): every raw-answer column pNNN scored against the key the manual prints under that wording reproduces bNNN exactly (agreement 1.000 for 24/24) and no other problem does (max off-diagonal 0.965); the live table equals the package b-columns cell for cell (10188 non-missing cells). Wording: verbatim from probability.Rd with two disclosed normalisations: the Rd source's double spaces after full stops were collapsed to single spaces, and the manual's prefatory '(Correct: 0.40)'-style keys were moved to correct_response. The source typo in p210 ('large or small The probability', missing full stop) is kept as printed. correct_response (key_source=source_published) transcribes the manual's printed answers; for b109/b209 the manual gives no number, only 'Responses that round to 0.06 were considered correct.', which ships verbatim. option_text 'error'/'correct' is the manual's own coding description for 0/1 (free numeric-response problems had no printed options). b110 carries two wordings by design: the manual prints 'The probability of drawing a red marble is 0.70 (lab: 0.30)' with key '(0.12, lab: 0.28)'; item_text ships the manual's sentence including the parenthetical rather than choosing one. The data confirm it: among the 26 lab respondents (ids 1-26, case l0001-l0026) 14 answered 0.28 and every one is scored correct, while 2 answering 0.12 are scored error; the online key reproduces lab b110 for only 8/26. The live IRW table carries no mode covariate, so lab rows are identifiable only by id 1-26. Language: the administered German questionnaire is not in the deposit (the pks package ships English wording only) and the paper could not be retrieved, so English ships in the base fields as translated_substitute. German is inferred, not stated: University of Tuebingen sample, German field-of-study coding, a 32-card (Skat/Piquet) deck and euro-cent coins. translation_source=study_supplied because the English is the data collectors'/package authors' own rendering (Wickelmaier collected the data and co-authors pks). Rights: the problems are the study authors' own items shipped in a GPL (>= 2) CRAN package; no restriction on the wording found. Not a register instrument. table_context.R printed a Sheet1 STOP (links populated to a hand-built sheet 1UEV3EG-6s4f-NombT3OVGaldTmWrG_ZBpahntgyFBJc). Overridden, Ben to confirm, same shape as batch_424-426: no pks item text is live (irw_list_itemtext_tables() has no pks table); the sheet's items tab carries the same manual wording (b110 given only as the online 0.70 variant, keys as 0.4 etc.), instrument = the dictionary Description, section 'main', and no option_text. If the STOP should hold, drop this CSV.
public_note: Problem b110 was worded differently for the 26 lab respondents (ids 1-26: red-marble probability 0.30, correct answer 0.28) than for the 478 online respondents (0.70, correct answer 0.12), and the English wording is the package authors' rendering of a questionnaire presumably administered in German.

note: Re-audit lead (irw#2382) said the Italian wording was not in the deposit and proposed the English canonical fallback; that was wrong about the paper: Table 2 prints all 12 Italian items with item number and component, plus the Italian instructions, so the administered wording ships (text_source=study_materials, language=Italian) with Neff's official English SCS-SF in the _translated columns. Italian transcribed from Table 2 verbatim, no final periods (as printed); one deviation: the line-break hyphenation 'emozi-oni' (item 7) is joined to 'emozioni'. The wording is NOT identical to the Neff-hosted Italian 26-item SCS (Veneziani, Fuochi & Voci 2017; self-compassion.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/ItalianSCS.pdf, sha256 bbe4585b...05e05c6) the paper says it drew from: items 1 and 8 read 'di importante per me' (long form 'che è importante per me'), item 9 'e fissarmi' (long form 'e a fissarmi'), item 10 'Quando mi sento inadeguato/a, in qualche modo cerco' (long form 'Quando mi sento in qualche modo inadeguato/a, cerco'). Table 2 (this study) is shipped as the administered text. Anchors: Table 2's instruction '1 = Quasi mai a 5 = Quasi sempre'; points 2-4 unlabelled and left blank. English twin: item_text_translated, option_text_translated ('Almost never'/'Almost always') and instructions_translated are Neff's official SCS-SF English verbatim (item 8 has no final period in Neff's PDF, kept); instructions_translated is Neff's instruction block, a parallel version rather than a word-for-word rendering of the Italian (which adds the 1/5 anchor sentence). Code derivation: the IRW codes are the deposit's own column names OI1..SJ2 lower-cased (pattern 1, no positional step), but those names carry subscale plus within-subscale ordinal, not item number, so the item-number tie was reconstructed: the same deposit's per-sample files name the columns by item number sc1..sc12, and joining them person-by-person to the live table reproduces each code on exactly one sc column (see verification). Rights: register row 'Self-Compassion Scale Short Form' (verdict ship; Neff: 'for any purpose whatsoever'), applied; see notes_ for the translation clause and why it is not read as a block. Instrument check (Step 3b): 12 items, 1-5, codes OI/SK/M/I/CH/SJ x2 = SCS-SF, matches.

This table is not distinguishable from that ruling: its live items cast_7p, cast_8p, cast_9p, cast_10p, cast_11p are CAST-18 items 7-11 (the Direct-Physical subscale) in CAST-18 numbering, and the wording in OSF 46pg7 Study 6/Measures/CAST.pdf (https://osf.io/download/9sp23/, sha256 98e1391fbf4838c3c014aed459747575ed67cdd88259ea2eb92fc5bd9f6b508e) is the full 18-item CAST (6 Direct-Verbal + 5 Direct-Physical + 7 Vicarious; e.g. physical 1 'I enjoy physically hurting people.', 5 'I enjoy hurting my partner during sex (or pretending to).'), character-identical to cast_7p..cast_11p in the held hyatt table. The irw#2382 lead's rights basis for this table ('silence': erinbuckels.com CAST-12 page sha256 89370af5..., unpublished 2014 manual, no PsycTESTS record) is the SAME evidence batch_311 recorded for hyatt, which Ben then ruled HOLD, so the lead's OBTAINABLE verdict is superseded. A 5-item subset of a held instrument is still the held wording, and the study's own OSF copy does not change whose wording it is (whose-page-governs rule). CAST.pdf itself carries no licence or terms. The block does reach something here: the item codes (cast_7p..) carry no wording, so the response table does not already expose the text. No CSV written; no register row written (the CAST hold lives in round_log rulings, not instrument_rights_register.csv, which has no CAST row). RETRY TEST: NO - an unchanged retry would reach the same determinate verdict. What would have to change: a human rights decision (Ben) lifting the CAST hold, e.g. a written grant from Buckels/Paulhus or a public CAST-18 release with no reserved right, recorded as a register row; then extraction is trivial (5 items, paper_explicit from CAST.pdf, codes CAST_#P per the Study 6 .csv headers). | DATA FINDINGS (response table, not item text): (1) one out-of-range response: resp=8 on a 1-7 scale, id 10, cast_7p, cov_study=study4 (live resp set 1..8; every other cell 1..7) - the same shape as hyatt's .sav coding CAST_7P point 6 as 8; likely a source miscode, check Study 4's raw CSV before trusting it. (2) id collision across stacked studies: 4,689 rows, 940 distinct (id, cov_study) units but only 268 distinct ids (study2 264, study4 165, study5 258, study6 253); 1,334 (id,item) keys repeat 2-4 times (68x2, 517x3, 749x4). data/west_2021_retaliatory_aggression.py sets id from each study's participant column without a study prefix; per the id-collision convention, id should be prefixed by study.
